prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-04-23. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 2.04 |
| Retained earnings       | 39,480M |
| Current liabilities     | 34,138M |
| Current assets          | 69,748M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 84,113M |
| Total liabilities       | 58,979M |
| Total assets            | 143,724M |
| EBIT / operating income | 941M |
| Revenue                 | 22,387M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-04-23, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The balance sheet shows solid liquidity (current ratio >2) and capitalization (equity > total liabilities, retained earnings nearly half of equity), but the income statement reveals very thin operating margins (EBIT/revenue ≈4%) and negligible return on assets, indicating limited debt-service capacity and placing the credit in the upper speculative-grade range.
DECISION: BB+
